source_note: Captured via F2 on 2026-09-12 while playing arcade Mortal Kombat II.
roi_reason: Added 2026-10-11: hashed over the whole frame, mk2__press_start_to_kontinue and mk2__prepare_for_next_kombat were only 20 bits apart (match threshold 24) - the shared MK II backdrop dominated the hash, so a slightly different live frame of one could be read as the other. Cropped to Player 1's panel, where the two actually differ, they're 78 bits apart. Caught by tests/test_screen_library.py::test_no_two_screens_are_confusable.
notes: Continue-countdown screen: Player 1's panel (left, red text) reads 'PRESS START TO KONTINUE'; a Player 2 panel at the right capture edge reads something starting 'PRESS...JO...' (likely 'PRESS START TO JOIN', green text) but is cut off - left out of canonical_text. See mk2__prepare_for_next_kombat for the other state this same panel was seen in.
